Stop car immediately to prevent warped engine heads. - TPMS Warning (Exclamation Mark in Horseshoe): One or more tires have low air pressure. - ABS Warning Light: Anti-lock braking system deactivated; standard brakes still function, but wheel lockup protection is disabled.

category: SECTION 11: FUEL TYPES, OCTANE RATINGS & EXHAUST ADDITIVES
question: Automotive knowledge regarding SECTION 11: FUEL TYPES, OCTANE RATINGS & EXHAUST ADDITIVES
answer: 11.1 Gasoline Octane Ratings (RON 91, RON 95, RON 98) - Definition: Research Octane Number (RON) measures gasoline's resistance to premature detonation ("engine knocking"). - Usage: Standard cars run on RON 91/95. High-performance turbocharged or high-compression engines require RON 98 to prevent engine knock. - Gasohol Blends (E10, E20, E85): Gasoline blended with ethanol alcohol. E10 contains 10% ethanol; E85 contains 85% ethanol (requires Flex-Fuel engine compatibility).

question: Automotive knowledge regarding SECTION 12: SAFETY RATINGS & DRIVER ASSISTANCE (ADAS)
answer: 11.2 Diesel Fuel & AdBlue (DEF - Diesel Exhaust Fluid) - Diesel Fuel (Euro 5 / Euro 6): Low-sulfur diesel fuel designed for modern high-pressure common rail diesel engines. - AdBlue / DEF: Non-toxic urea solution injected into diesel exhaust systems (SCR - Selective Catalytic Reduction) to convert harmful Nitrogen Oxide (NOx) pollutants into harmless nitrogen and water vapor. 12.1 Euro NCAP Safety Rating (1 to 5 Stars)

question: Automotive knowledge regarding SECTION 12: SAFETY RATINGS & DRIVER ASSISTANCE (ADAS)
answer: - Definition: European New Car Assessment Programme rating assessing adult occupant protection, child occupant protection, vulnerable road user protection, and safety assist technologies. - 5 Stars: Overall excellent performance in crash protection and collision avoidance technology. 12.2 ADAS Autonomy Levels (Level 0 to Level 5) - Level 0: No automation; human driver controls all functions (warnings only).

question: Automotive knowledge regarding SECTION 12: SAFETY RATINGS & DRIVER ASSISTANCE (ADAS)
answer: - Level 1: Driver Assistance; single system assists with steering OR acceleration/braking (e.g., standard Cruise Control). - Level 2: Partial Automation; system controls steering AND acceleration simultaneously under driver supervision (e.g., Adaptive Cruise Control with Lane Centering). - Level 3: Conditional Automation; vehicle handles driving tasks in specific conditions (e.g., traffic jam pilot), driver must be ready to take over. - Level 4: High Automation; vehicle drives autonomously in designated areas without driver intervention.

question: Automotive knowledge regarding SECTION 12: SAFETY RATINGS & DRIVER ASSISTANCE (ADAS)
answer: - Level 5: Full Automation; complete driverless vehicle in all conditions. 12.3 Active vs Passive Safety Systems - Active Systems: ABS, ESP/ESC, AEB (Autonomous Emergency Braking), BSM (Blind Spot Monitoring), Lane Keep Assist (LKA). - Passive Systems: Crumple Zones, Airbags (Front, Side, Curtain, Knee), Isofix Child Seat Anchors, Seatbelt Pre-tensioners.

question: Automotive knowledge regarding SECTION 13: DRIVING MODES & CONVENIENCE TECHNOLOGIES
answer: 13.1 Driving Modes (Eco, Comfort, Sport, Snow/Off-Road) - Eco Mode: Softens throttle sensitivity, shifts gear early, and optimizes climate control to maximize fuel economy. - Comfort / Normal Mode: Balanced suspension softness, steering weight, and smooth throttle response for daily driving. - Sport / Sport+ Mode: Sharpens throttle response, holds engine gears at higher RPM, stiffens adaptive suspension, and increases steering weight for aggressive driving.

question: Automotive knowledge regarding SECTION 13: DRIVING MODES & CONVENIENCE TECHNOLOGIES
answer: - Snow / Mud / Sand Mode: Adjusts traction control and wheel torque slip to maintain grip on loose surfaces. 13.2 Driver Convenience Features - Electronic Parking Brake (EPB): Replaces manual handbrake lever with a push-button electronic switch. - Auto Hold Function: Holds brake hydraulic pressure automatically when the vehicle comes to a complete stop at traffic lights, allowing the driver to remove their foot from the brake pedal until pressing the accelerator.

question: Automotive knowledge regarding SECTION 14: MARKET SEGMENTS (A-SEGMENT TO F-SEGMENT)
answer: - Hill Start Assist (HSA): Automatically holds brake pressure for 2–3 seconds when starting on a steep uphill slope, preventing the car from rolling backward. - Paddle Shifters: Steering-wheel-mounted levers (+/-) allowing manual gear override on automatic or dual-clutch transmissions. - Segment A (City Cars / Microcars): Ultra-compact urban cars (e.g., Fiat 500, Hyundai i10, Toyota Aygo). - Segment B (Subcompact / Small Cars): Small hatchbacks and crossovers (e.g., VW Polo, Renault Clio, Ford Fiesta).

question: Automotive knowledge regarding SECTION 14: MARKET SEGMENTS (A-SEGMENT TO F-SEGMENT)
answer: - Segment C (Compact / Medium Cars): Family hatchbacks, sedans, compact SUVs (e.g., VW Golf, Toyota Corolla, Honda Civic). - Segment D (Midsize / Executive Cars): Midsize sedans and crossovers (e.g., BMW 3 Series, Audi A4, VW Passat). - Segment E (Full-size Executive / Luxury Cars): Large luxury sedans (e.g., BMW 5 Series, Mercedes-Benz E-Class, Audi A6). - Segment F (Ultra-Luxury / Flagship / Supercars): Flagship luxury sedans, supercars, hypercars (e.g., Mercedes-Maybach, BMW 7 Series, Porsche 911, Ferrari, Lamborghini).

category: SECTION 15: CAR BUYING, DEPRECIATION & TOTAL COST OF OWNERSHIP (TCO)
question: Automotive knowledge regarding SECTION 15: CAR BUYING, DEPRECIATION & TOTAL COST OF OWNERSHIP (TCO)
answer: 15.1 Financial & Pricing Terms - Base MSRP (Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price): The recommended starting base price before optional equipment, taxes, and dealer fees. - OTR Price (On-The-Road Price): Total final price including taxes, registration fees, insurance, and delivery charges. - Depreciation: The loss in market value of a vehicle over time. Cars typically lose 15%–25% of value in their first year.

category: SECTION 15: CAR BUYING, DEPRECIATION & TOTAL COST OF OWNERSHIP (TCO)
question: Automotive knowledge regarding SECTION 15: CAR BUYING, DEPRECIATION & TOTAL COST OF OWNERSHIP (TCO)
answer: - Resale Value: Remaining market value of a used vehicle when sold after several years of ownership. 15.2 Ownership Economics & Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) - Total Cost of Ownership (TCO): The overall expense of owning a vehicle over 3–5 years, calculating: TCO = Purchase Price + Depreciation + Fuel/Energy Cost + Maintenance/Repairs + Insurance + Taxes - Resale Value

category: SECTION 15: CAR BUYING, DEPRECIATION & TOTAL COST OF OWNERSHIP (TCO)
question: Automotive knowledge regarding SECTION 15: CAR BUYING, DEPRECIATION & TOTAL COST OF OWNERSHIP (TCO)
answer: - EV vs ICE Ownership Economics: Pure electric vehicles (BEVs) generally have higher upfront purchase prices (MSRP), but deliver significantly lower fuel/energy costs and up to 40% lower routine maintenance costs (no engine oil changes, spark plugs, timing belts, or exhaust system repairs).
